description: A room block whose #dig designations carry explicit dig priorities so the miners open the fort in a sensible order instead of scattering across every tile at once. The central column is the trunk corridor
column4: so it is mined first and becomes a highway the moment digging starts. The four single tiles marked d2 (priority 2) are the doorways that punch from each room into that corridor
column5: dug second once the highway exists. The four 3x3 rooms are all d3 (priority 3)
column6: hollowed out last after access is guaranteed. A dig token is the letter d followed by a priority number from 1 to 7
column7: where 1 is dug first and 7 last; a bare number like 3 means the same as d3
column8: and leaving the number off (a plain d) defaults to priority 4. Priorities also work with the compact extent form
column9: so d3(3x3) would stamp a whole room at priority 3 from one anchor cell. Priorities never change WHAT gets dug
column11: so this blueprint carves exactly the same tiles as one written with plain d everywhere; it just keeps your miners on the corridor first so the rooms are reachable the moment they are opened.
